claim: The Ducasse d'Ath is held annually on the fourth Sunday of August, featuring processional giants including Mr and Mrs Goliath and the horse Bayard; it marks David's victory over Goliath.
quote: annually on the fourth Sunday of August... Mr and Mrs Goliath (the central figures), Bayard (a legendary horse), Ambiorix

claim: The Ducasse d'Ath was inscribed by UNESCO in 2008 as part of the Processional Giants and Dragons of Belgium and France, but was delisted in December 2022 after complaints about a blackface character.
quote: delisted in December 2022 following complaints about one of the characters that appears in the procession

claim: The 2026 Ducasse d'Ath is officially scheduled for the weekend of 21-24 August 2026.
Maison des Géants in Ath is a dedicated museum interpreting the city's giant-processional tradition; it opens Tue–Fri 10–17 and Sat–Sun 14–18, closed Mondays.
quote: Tuesday to Friday from 10am to 5pm, Saturdays and Sundays from 2pm to 6pm

claim: Maison des Géants admission is €6 adult, €5.50 senior, €5 child/student; free on the first Sunday of each month and for under-5s.
quote: Adult admission is €6, seniors (60+) are €5.50, children and students are €5... Every first Sunday of the month, the museum opens its doors free of charge

claim: Château d'Attre near Ath (Brugelette) is an 18th-century castle still privately inhabited, set in a listed park with a fabriqued 'rocher', visitable Sunday afternoons spring–autumn and Saturdays in summer.
quote: The castle can be visited every Sunday afternoon from spring to autumn, and also on summer Saturdays

claim: Hôpital Notre-Dame à la Rose in Lessines opens Tue–Fri 9:00–18:00 (last entry 16:45) and Sat/Sun/holidays 9:30–18:30 (last entry 17:15), closed Mondays except public holidays.
quote: Tuesday-Friday: 9am-6pm (last entry 4:45pm); Saturday, Sunday & Public Holidays: 9:30am-6:30pm (last entry 5:15pm); Closed Mondays

claim: Notre-Dame à la Rose is one of the oldest hospitals in Europe, founded in 1242 by Alix de Rosoit, with an intact ensemble of Baroque chapel, cloister, medicinal gardens, sick ward and convent.
quote: One of the oldest hospitals in Europe... A majestic and authentic architectural ensemble... Baroque chapel, cloister, medicinal gardens, sick ward, and convent

claim: The Lessines hospital operated continuously until the 1980s before becoming a museum with about 20 scenographied rooms covering medicine from the Middle Ages to today.
quote: the hospital operated until the 1980s, and has since been transformed into a museum

claim: Notre-Dame Cathedral in Tournai has been a UNESCO World Heritage site since 2000, distinguished by a Romanesque nave, transept topped by five towers, and a Gothic choir completed 1254.
quote: Romanesque nave of extraordinary dimensions, a wealth of sculpture on its capitals and a transept topped by five towers, all precursors of the Gothic style

claim: Tournai Cathedral is open daily; the Treasury costs €2.50 (€2 group/senior) and is open Mon–Fri 10:00–18:00 and weekends 14:30–18:00.
quote: Treasury Room: €2.50 per person (€2.00 for groups/seniors)

claim: The Belfry of Tournai is open to individuals 13:30–17:30 except Mondays; private morning guided tours by reservation.
quote: Individuals can visit from 1:30 p.m. to 5:30 p.m. (except for Mondays)

claim: Tournai's Belfry, begun in 1188, stands 72 m tall with a 256-step stairway and was inscribed by UNESCO in 1999 as part of the Belfries of Belgium and France; it is the oldest belfry in Belgium.
quote: 72 metres (236 feet) tall and features a 256-step stairway... inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List in 1999

claim: Road distance from Baudour to Tournai is about 39.9 km / 30 minutes — just outside the strict 30 km radius.
quote: The driving distance between Tournai and Baudour is 39.9 km (24.8 miles)

claim: Road distance Baudour to Lessines is about 33 km / 37 minutes; Ath to Lessines is ~11 km / 9 minutes.
quote: Lessines to Baudour: The driving distance is 33.3 km (20.7 mi) with an estimated travel time of 37 minutes

claim: Baudour to Ath is roughly 22 km / 23 minutes by car, comfortably inside the 30 km radius.
quote: The distance by road between Ath and Baudour is 13.8 miles (approximately 22 kilometers). It takes approximately 23 minutes
